arxiv-2212-05923.title: Self-Supervised Object Goal Navigation with In-Situ Finetuning
arxiv-2212-05923.creator: So Yeon Min, Yao-Hung Hubert Tsai, Wei Ding, Ali Farhadi, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Yonatan Bisk, Jian Zhang
arxiv-2212-05923.description: Abstract A household robot should be able to navigate to target objects without requiring users to first annotate everything in their home. Most current approaches to object navigation do not test on real robots and rely solely on reconstructed scans of houses and their expensively labeled semantic 3D meshes.

arxiv-2405-11472.title: Signatures of the Attractive Interaction in Spin Spectra of One-Dimensional Cuprate Chains
arxiv-2405-11472.creator: Zecheng Shen, Jiarui Liu, Hao-Xin Wang, Yao Wang
arxiv-2405-11472.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Zecheng Shen, Jiarui Liu, Hao-Xin Wang, Yao Wang. Identifying the minimal model for cuprates is crucial for explaining the high- T c T_{c} pairing mechanism. Recent photoemission experiments have suggested a significant near-neighbor attractive interaction V V in cuprate chains, favoring pairing instability. To determine its strength, we systematically investigate the dynamical spin structure factors S ⁡ ( q , ω ) S(q,\omega) using the density matrix renormalization group.

arxiv-2407-20544.title: Automated Physical Design Watermarking Leveraging Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2407-20544.creator: Ruisi Zhang, Rachel Selina Rajarathnam, David Z. Pan, Farinaz Koushanfar
arxiv-2407-20544.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Ruisi Zhang, Rachel Selina Rajarathnam, David Z. Pan, Farinaz Koushanfar. This paper presents AutoMarks , an automated and transferable watermarking framework that leverages graph neural networks to reduce the watermark search overheads during the placement stage.

arxiv-2502-11478.title: TAPS: Throat and Acoustic Paired Speech Dataset for Deep Learning-Based Speech Enhancement
arxiv-2502-11478.creator: Yunsik Kim, Yonghun Song, Yoonyoung Chung
arxiv-2502-11478.description: Abstract In high-noise environments such as factories, subways, and busy streets, capturing clear speech is challenging due to background noise. Throat microphones provide a solution with their noise-suppressing properties, reducing the noise while recording speech. However, a significant limitation remains: high-frequency information is attenuated as sound waves pass through skin and tissue, reducing speech clarity.

arxiv-2508-00993.title: Consistent DAG selection for Bayesian Causal Discovery under general error distributions
arxiv-2508-00993.creator: Anamitra Chaudhuri, Anirban Bhattacharya, Yang Ni
arxiv-2508-00993.description: Abstract We consider the problem of learning the underlying causal structure among a set of variables, which are assumed to follow a Bayesian network or, more specifically, a linear recursive structural equation model (SEM) with the associated errors being independent and allowed to be non-Gaussian.

arxiv-2508-17056.title: TabResFlow: A Normalizing Spline Flow Model for Probabilistic Univariate Tabular Regression
arxiv-2508-17056.creator: Kiran Madhusudhanan, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi, Jonas Sonntag, Maximilian Stubbemann, Lars Schmidt-Thieme
arxiv-2508-17056.description: Abstract Tabular regression is a well-studied problem with numerous industrial applications, yet most existing approaches focus on point estimation, often leading to overconfident predictions. This issue is particularly critical in industrial automation, where trustworthy decision-making is essential. Probabilistic regression models address this challenge by modeling prediction uncertainty.

arxiv-2512-24154.title: Mechanical properties of chiral actin filaments
arxiv-2512-24154.creator: Amir Khosravanizadeh, François Nédélec, Serge Dmitrieff
arxiv-2512-24154.description: Abstract The mechanical properties of actin filaments are essential to their biological functions. Here, we introduce a highly coarse-grained model of actin filaments that preserves helicity and chirality while enabling mesoscale simulations. The framework is implemented in Cytosim, an open-source cytoskeleton simulation platform.

arxiv-2601-04285.title: A Future Capabilities Agent for Tactical Air Traffic Control
arxiv-2601-04285.creator: Paul Kent, George De Ath, Martin Layton, Allen Hart, Richard Everson, Ben Carvell
arxiv-2601-04285.description: Abstract Escalating air traffic demand is driving the adoption of automation to support air traffic controllers, but existing approaches face a trade-off between safety assurance and interpretability. Optimisation-based methods such as reinforcement learning offer strong performance but are difficult to verify and explain, while rules-based systems are transparent yet rarely check safety under uncertainty.

pmc-10694946.title: Immunoproteasome function maintains oncogenic gene expression in KMT2A-complex driven leukemia
pmc-10694946.creator: Nuria Tubío-Santamaría, Ashok Kumar Jayavelu, Tina M Schnoeder, Theresa Eifert, Chen-Jen Hsu, Florian Perner, Qirui Zhang, Daniela V Wenge, Fynn M Hansen, Joanna M Kirkpatrick, Nidhi Jyotsana, Steven W Lane, Björn von Eyss, Aniruddha J Deshpande, Michael W M Kühn, Juerg Schwaller, Clemens Cammann, U
pmc-10694946.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Pharmacologic targeting of chromatin-associated protein complexes has shown significant responses in KMT2A-rearranged (KMT2A-r) acute myeloid leukemia (AML) but resistance frequently develops to single agents. This points to a need for therapeutic combinations that target multiple mechanisms. To enhance our understanding of functional dependencies in KMT2A-r AML, we have used a proteomic approach to identify the catalytic immunoproteasome subunit PSMB8 as a specific vulnerability.

pmc-11415708.title: Terminal sequence consistency verification method for small diameter abreast optical fibers based on computer vision
pmc-11415708.creator: Yan Wang, Lei Wang, Dalin Li, Yanchun Liang, Lan Huang, Haoming Da, Hui Yang
pmc-11415708.description: In a kind of precision industrial equipment, small diameter abreast optical fibers are used for high-speed communication among functional nodes. The arrangement order at both terminals of the abreast optical fibers need to comply with communication protocols. In this paper, we propose an automatic terminal sequence consistency verification method based on computer vision.

pmc-11418123.title: Structure of a truncated human GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase variant reveals the basis for its hyperactivity
pmc-11418123.creator: Hua Li, Balraj Doray, Benjamin C Jennings, Wang-Sik Lee, Lin Liu, Stuart Kornfeld, Huilin Li
pmc-11418123.description: Mutations that cause loss of function of GlcNAc-1-phosphotransferase (PTase) lead to the lysosomal storage disorder mucolipidosis II. PTase is the key enzyme of the mannose 6-phosphate (M6P) targeting system that is responsible for tagging lysosomal hydrolases with the M6P moiety for their delivery to the lysosome.

pmc-11557002.title: Primary clear cell adenocarcinoma of the seminal vesicle with ovarian homology: A rare case report
pmc-11557002.creator: Yang Yuan, Yunlong Li, Shihao Zhang, Dingli Hu, Song Xu, Tingting Gu
pmc-11557002.description: Rationale:Primary seminal vesicle adenocarcinoma is a rare type of male reproductive system tumor, primarily manifesting as papillary adenocarcinoma. Meanwhile, clear cell adenocarcinoma (CCA) is a common malignancy in the female reproductive system. Therefore, the occurrence of CCA in the seminal vesicle, showing ovarian homology, is even rarer. This pathological type of seminal vesicle cancer has been seldom reported.

pmc-12502641.title: Analysis of clinicopathological features and clinical significance in 25 cases of mammary adenoid cystic carcinoma
pmc-12502641.creator: Xiaoyan Xu, Shasha Yu, Wei Qu, Yuexia Chen, Liu Yang
pmc-12502641.description: BackgroundMammary adenoid cystic carcinoma (AdCC) is a rare subtype of invasive breast cancer. Due to its low incidence, the clinicopathological features of mammary AdCC remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to investigate the clinicopathological and molecular characteristics, therapeutic regimens, and prognostic outcomes associated with different subtypes of mammary AdCC.

pmc-12533928.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Conversational Agents to Improve Patient Experience Related to Physicians: Cross-Sectional Study in China
pmc-12533928.creator: Dehe Li, Heman Zhang, Chuntao Lu, Chunxia Miao, Alicia Stone
pmc-12533928.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence-assisted conversational agents have been applied and developed in outpatient departments to improve health services in China. However, there has been little research that evaluates the effect of artificial intelligence-assisted conversational agents on the patient experience related to physicians during outpatient visits.

pmc-12542520.title: Cell-cycle-related transcriptional factor DLX4: a novel prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target in colorectal cancer
pmc-12542520.creator: Jingsong Cheng, Chengxi Zhang, Yiman Luo, Yihan Chen, Nanting Chen, Yuanyuan Wan, Xinyu Huang, Ziheng Zheng, Qingyao Yin, Xue Chen, Jing Hua, Yang Li, Rongzhong Huang
pmc-12542520.description: Distal - less homeobox 4 (DLX4) is a transcription factor vital for embryonic development and shows pro - oncogenic properties in some hematological and solid tumors. In colorectal cancer (CRC), its molecular function and contributions to tumorigenesis remain to be explored.

pmc-12794806.title: Safety and Efficacy of Ozanimod in Patients With Moderately to Severely Active Ulcerative Colitis Stratified by Age
pmc-12794806.creator: Adam S Faye, David T Rubin, Corey A Siegel, Millie D Long, Nabeel Khan, Silvio Danese, Peter M Irving, Raymond K Cross, Irina Blumenstein, Alessandro Armuzzi, Sara N Horst, Axel Dignass, Taku Kobayashi, Garrett Lawlor, Anthony Krakovich, AnnKatrin Petersen, Zhaohui Liu, Dong Wang, Anjali Jain, Ashwi
pmc-12794806.description: Background:Older adults with ulcerative colitis (UC) have unique treatment challenges. Ozanimod is approved for the treatment of moderately to severely active UC in adults based on the phase 3 True North (TN) study results. Here, we analyzed the impact of patient age on ozanimod safety and efficacy in TN and during the open-label extension (OLE).

pmc-12957540.title: Versatile Nanotherapeutics for Enhancing Sonodynamic Therapy/Chemotherapy of Thyroid Cancer through Remodeling Tumor Microenvironment and Synergistic Reactive Oxygen Species Augment
pmc-12957540.creator: Dan Wang, Lei Sun, Juan Wang, Lirong Wang, Zhongyu Wang, Yutong Zhang, Qi Zhou, Yuhang Chen, Jue Jiang
pmc-12957540.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma (ATC), as the most malignant pathological type, is prone to local invasion and even distant metastasis with a poor prognosis and a high recurrence rate. Herein, we developed an iron-based metal organic framework (FL@M) as an effective sonosensitizer and biomimetic nanocarrier through the incorporation of lenvatinib (Len) and further coating with homologous tumor cell membranes, achieving the synergistic sonodynamic therapy/chemotherapy for ATC.

pmc-13243642.title: Organochlorine pesticide residues monitoring and human health risk evaluation in agricultural crops from Ilam Province, Southwest of Iran
pmc-13243642.creator: Ali Amarloei, Zahra Noorimotlagh, Neemat Jaafarzadeh, Seyyed Abbas Mirzaee
pmc-13243642.description: The issue of food supply and security remains a major challenge and crisis for the world’s growing population. In this study, a comprehensive analysis of the residues of fourteen organochlorine pesticides (OCPs) was conducted and detected using gas chromatography with an electron capture detector (GC/ECD) in sixty-one samples of twelve crops produced in ten counties within Ilam Province, southwest Iran.

pmc-13359387.title: Intravenous Dihydroxyacetone as Adjunctive Therapy in Aluminum Phosphide Poisoning: A Case Series
pmc-13359387.creator: Hossein Niknahad, Reza Heidari, Leila Hosseini, Shayan Yazdani, Hanif Hashemnejad, Mohammadreza Rahimi Majd
pmc-13359387.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In three patients with aluminum phosphide poisoning, intravenous dihydroxyacetone (DHA) was added to standard supportive care. Improvement in metabolic acidosis and hemodynamic status was temporally associated with DHA administration. Controlled studies are needed to determine efficacy and safety.Keywords: acute toxicity, dihydroxyacetone, emergency medicine, pharmacotherapy, phosphine Introduction Aluminum phosphide (AlP) poisoning is associated with high mortality (up to ~85%) and remains a major clinical problem in many agricultural regions, including Iran, India, Pakistan, and Turkey [1, 2, 3, 4].

pmc-13385629.title: Molecular MRI monitoring of cyclodextrin therapy in murine abdominal aortic aneurysms
pmc-13385629.creator: Jennifer L. Heyl, Dilyana B. Mangarova, Jana Möckel, Jennifer Mein, David Hingst, Uwe Karst, René M. Botnar, Lisa C. Adams, Marcus R. Makowski, Federico Collettini, Matthias Taupitz, Christa Thöne-Reineke, Bernd Hamm, Avan Kader, Julia Brangsch
pmc-13385629.description: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) are characterized by progressive extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation and inflammation of the aortic wall. 2-Hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (cyclodextrin) has shown potential in attenuating AAA progression via activation of transcription factor EB. This study evaluated whether molecular magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) enables non-invasive monitoring of therapeutic effects in a murine AAA model.

pmc-13471494.title: MSTM-Net: a two-stage prostate cancer segmentation network based on swin-transformer-mamba architecture
pmc-13471494.creator: Jiatao Chen, Xiang Liu, Shuohong Wang, Wenbin Ji
pmc-13471494.description: BackgroundMagnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has become a core imaging modality for prostate cancer screening and diagnosis. Accurate and automatic segmentation of lesion regions is critical for subsequent staging assessment and treatment planning.MethodsTo this end, this research proposes a two-stage segmentation framework for multimodal MRI.

pmc-13622896.title: Impact of playing position on ACL injury characteristics, risk and career outcomes in football—An analysis of 742 cases of the anterior cruciate ligament registry in German football
pmc-13622896.creator: Shoichi Hasegawa, Werner Krutsch, Hidejuki Koga, Volker Alt, Dominik Szymski, Lorenz Huber
pmc-13622896.description: PurpuseTo evaluate how playing position affects anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury features, incidence rates and career outcomes across competition levels in male football.MethodsUsing the prospectively collected ‘ACL Registry in German Football’, we analysed six seasons (2016–2022) across professional (first to third leagues), semi‐professional (fourth to sixth) and amateur (seventh) levels.
